questions.question: What is a regular expression?
explanations: Correct. A regular expression (regex) is a pattern used to search, validate or manipulate text.
No. It is not a type of variable; it is a search pattern.
No. It is not a sorting function.
No. It is not a control structure; it is a text pattern.

questions.question: How are regular expressions used in Java?
explanations: Correct. In Java, Pattern is used to compile the pattern and Matcher to perform the matches.
No. There are no Regex and Search classes in standard Java.
No. They are not classes; they are Matcher methods.
No. There are no Scan and Parse classes for regex.

questions.question: What does \d do in a regular expression?
explanations: Correct. \d is a metacharacter that matches any digit from 0 to 9.
No. For letters you use \w or classes like [a-zA-Z].
No. For any character you use the dot (.).

questions.question: What does the + operator do in a regular expression?
explanations: Correct. + means one or more occurrences of the previous pattern.
No. Zero or one occurrence is the ? operator.
No. There is no operator for exactly one; + means one or more.
No. There is no operator for zero occurrences.
